title: 2026 UK ETS SAF evidence and no-double-claim proposal QA controls

sources.title: Treatment of sustainable aviation fuel consultation accessible webpage

facts.source_fact: Current Article 54 allows analytical methods for physically mixed fossil fuel and biofuel batches.
Current rules allow purchase mass-balance evidence where analytical methods are unreasonably costly or technically infeasible.
The Authority proposes purchase and delivery records as the default evidence method.
The no-double-claiming requirement would be retained under the proposal.
SAF relied on for another regulatory emissions reduction or financial benefit cannot also support the same UK ETS claim under the proposal.
The consultation names CORSIA and EU ETS as examples of other schemes relevant to no-double-claiming evidence.
SAF transferred to another person cannot support the same claim under the no-double-claiming rule.
Evidence may be required by both verifier and regulator.
The proposed evidence change had not yet been enacted in the consultation source.
Evidence of SAF claims is compliance evidence, not parcel-level emissions measurement.
